# Notes, keys and numerals

Pitches are MIDI numbers, 60 = middle C. Onsets are slots 0 to 15 of a sixteenth grid, so slot 4 is beat 2; lengths are in beats. Tiers: M1 is needed in a first test set, M2 has one or two sources or is a jazz or world idiom, M3 is single-source, inferred or theory only. Tags: `source states`, `measured`, `derived` (our computation on public data), `inferred` (our reading), `snippet` (a search excerpt), `single source`, `proposal` (a policy, not a fact). Source ids are listed in `dictionary/sources.json`.

## Middle-C labels

A program labels note 60 C3, C4 or C5. Ask the producer which label their program shows before reading a note name; store MIDI numbers.

| MIDI | Label C4 (scientific) | Label C3 | Label C5 |
| --: | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| 21 | A0 | A-1 | A1 |
| 28 | E1 | E0 | E2 |
| 36 | C2 | C1 | C3 |
| 60 | C4 | C3 | C5 |
| 69 | A4 | A3 | A5 |
| 127 | G9 | G8 | G10 |

Octave number of MIDI `n`: `n div 12 - 1` with label C4, `n div 12 - 2` with C3, `n div 12` with C5. Frequency: `440 * 2^((n - 69) / 12)` Hz.

## Camelot and Open Key

The same number with the other letter is the relative key; one number up or down is a fifth; 12 wraps to 1.

| Camelot | Minor (A) | Major (B) | Open Key |
| --: | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| 1 | G# minor | B major | 6m and 6d |
| 2 | D# minor | F# major | 7m and 7d |
| 3 | Bb minor | Db major | 8m and 8d |
| 4 | F minor | Ab major | 9m and 9d |
| 5 | C minor | Eb major | 10m and 10d |
| 6 | G minor | Bb major | 11m and 11d |
| 7 | D minor | F major | 12m and 12d |
| 8 | A minor | C major | 1m and 1d |
| 9 | E minor | G major | 2m and 2d |
| 10 | B minor | D major | 3m and 3d |
| 11 | F# minor | A major | 4m and 4d |
| 12 | C# minor | E major | 5m and 5d |
